source.title: Maximum K to Sort a Permutation

teaching.hint: What restriction does every value that must move impose on the bits of `k`?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Every misplaced value must participate in a swap, so `k` is bounded by their bitwise AND; that bound is attainable using its own value as a universal swap partner.
solution_outline.approach: AND together the values not at their final indices. For the resulting `K`, the permutation contains value `K`, which can swap with each misplaced value because `K & x = K`.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: `K` is a submask of every misplaced value; star swaps through the element `K` connect all values that must be permuted.
solution_outline.correctness: Any feasible `k` is a submask of every value that moves, hence no greater than `K`. Star swaps through `K` generate every permutation of the relevant values, including one restoring sorted order, so `K` is feasible.
solution_outline.pitfall: Including already-correct values in the AND can lower the answer even though they need not move.

common_wrong_turns: ANDing all values including fixed points
Assuming the pivot cannot move temporarily
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained permutation guarantee, value-based swap condition, and the sorted-array special result.
